subject: Wage Theft Prevention and Demolition Delay Extension
overview: The Council adopted a Wage Theft Prevention Ordinance and advanced an amendment to significantly extend the demolition delay for historic properties. The meeting also included the vetting of several Community Preservation Committee members and funding authorizations for new election equipment and fire safety gear.

items.title: Wage Theft Prevention Ordinance
items.summary: Approved the third reading of the Wage Theft Prevention Ordinance to ensure public contractors comply with wage and hour laws.

items.title: Sign Variance at 25 Hall Street
items.summary: Approved a sign size variance for George's Bakery to fit the architecture of the building.

items.title: Community Preservation Committee Vetting
items.summary: Vetted and approved the appointments of Joan Cyr, Elizabeth Cary Soul, Joseph Pecora, and Roberta Cameron to the Community Preservation Committee.

items.title: Historic District Establishment at 21 Turo Avenue
items.summary: Approved the establishment of a local historic district at 21 Turo Avenue to preserve the property and prevent subdivision.

items.title: Demolition Delay Ordinance Amendment
items.summary: Passed the first reading of an amendment to Chapter 48 to extend the demolition delay from 6 months to 18 months for buildings 75 years or older. Residents and the Historical Commission argued that the current delay was ineffective against developers waiting out the time frame to demolish significant structures.

items.title: Citywide Street Sweeping Program
items.summary: Referred a proposal for permanent street sweeping signage and staggered parking to the Public Works Subcommittee for further review.

items.title: Election Equipment and Fire Department Funding
items.summary: Approved an expenditure from free cash for new voting machines, amended to include $29,700 for the purchase of turnout gear extractors and dryers for the fire department.

items.title: Water and Sewer Connectivity Charge
items.summary: Referred a discussion regarding a proposed bimonthly fixed connectivity charge for water and sewer rates to a Committee of the Whole meeting on May 2nd.

items.title: EpiPens for First Responders
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting the administration to examine the feasibility of providing EpiPens and relevant training to city first responders.

items.title: Food Establishment Grading System
items.summary: Approved a request for the Board of Health to examine a grading system for food establishments, including an update on the status of the current inspection backlog.

items.title: Municipal Aggregation and Bus Stop Safety
items.summary: Placed on file a resident petition against municipal aggregation and approved a request for a DOT report on the T bus stop at Main and High Street.
